principles: Order by full-length bars (4m/5m/6m) as priced in the materials pricebook.
Convert cut pieces into bar counts using greedy bin packing per profile.
Choose non-continuous stock by the lowest total purchase cost, then least waste and fewest bars.
Do not assume offcut reuse across different jobs (conservative true-cost).
Track and report offcuts as waste for the job; optionally keep for internal salvage later.
algorithm_outline: For each profile, build a list of required cut lengths (m) from derived quantities and detailing rules.
For each available stock length for that profile (from the pricebook), arrange the required cuts and calculate whole bars, total purchase cost and waste.
For continuous runs, preserve the existing splice-minimising selection rule.
For non-continuous cuts, select the lowest total purchase cost, then least waste, then fewest bars, then lowest cost per metre.
Sort cut lengths descending; place each length into the first bar with enough remaining length; otherwise start a new bar.
Compute bars_used, total_stock_length, total_cut_length, waste_length = total_stock_length - total_cut_length.
If waste_allowance_percent > 0, inflate bars_used by that % (rounded up) and recompute waste.
